items.title: South Africa mine collapse kills 14 suspected illegal miners
items.description: At least 14 suspected illegal miners were killed and eight injured when a mine dump collapsed in South Africa.

items.title: WHO: DRC Ebola outbreak began months before it was officially declared
items.description: The Ebola outbreak in the DR Congo began months before it was officially declared, the World Health Organization told a news conference in Bunia on Monday. It’s now the fastest growing Ebola outbreak on record.

items.title: Cargo ship in flames after Houthi attack in Bab al-Mandeb strait
items.description: Footage shows an Egyptian-owned cargo vessel in flames in the Bab al-Mandeb strait after a suspected Houthi attack.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez tie the knot after 10 years
items.description: They married on Tuesday in a civil ceremony described by the public relations team that represents the Portuguese soccer star as ‘a private and intimate moment attended by their five children’

items.title: South Africa weather alert: snow, hail and icy roads disrupt travel
items.description: Heavy snow, hail, rain and icy conditions are causing major disruption across several provinces in South Africa, with a number of key roads closed. Motorists are being urged to drive with extreme caution.

items.title: Trump says Iran options are let Tehran fail economically or ‘hit them really hard’
items.description: ‘We control their money, what they ⁠had, which is a lot; they had a lot, and we have total control of it; I’m ‌their banker,’ said Donald Trump, referring to frozen Iranian assets

items.title: Russia releases former US Marine reported in poor health
items.description: Robert Gilman, who was arrested in 2022, was left in "life-threatening condition" after being subjected to "harsh and abusive treatment", his family says.

items.title: Quintela and the Peronists; Weird scarecrow strategy
items.description: Most Argentines are telling pollsters that they would like something to change next year. But polls measuring voting intention still have Milei either in the lead or neck-and-neck with his main opponent. Leer más

items.title: The Office star Lucy Davis announces she has incurable cancer
items.description: Actress Lucy Davis, best known for her role as Dawn Tinsley on the UK version of The Office, says she has "incurable" stage 4 breast cancer.

items.title: Argentina designates three Ecuador gangs as ‘terrorist groups’
items.description: Milei and Noboa sign security, trade and extradition agreements during talks in Quito; Los Lobos, Los Choneros and Chone Killers designated as terrorist groups. Leer más

items.title: Argentina prison watchdog flags overcrowding and detainee rights concerns
items.description: Argentina’s PPN federal prison watchdog warns of overcrowding, lack of transparency and rights setbacks in annual report. Leer más

items.title: Thousands march in Argentina on Day of San Cayetano, patron saint of bread and work
items.description: Traditional pilgrimage to patron saint of bread and work doubles as protest against Milei’s austerity measures. Leer más

items.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy makes first visit to Russia-friendly Serbia
items.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is making his first visit to Serbia. His host, President Aleksandar Vucic, hopes to score points with the EU, while Zelenskyy seeks more arms from a country that remains friendly to Russia.

items.title: Vietnam's VinSpace taps SpaceX for first satellite launches
items.description: Vietnam's first private space company is turning to Elon Musk's SpaceX to get its first satellites into orbit. The deal comes as Vietnam steps up efforts to build its own space industry and become a regional space power.

items.title: Anguish of Colombian brother at rubble of building being searched for earthquake survivors
items.description: BBC Mundo has gone to the site of Torres del Limonar, a collapsed building in Cali where rescue workers fight to free survivors.

items.title: Sierra Leone president presses lawmakers to back contested election reforms
items.description: Sierra Leone’s President Julius Maada Bio has urged Parliament to pass disputed electoral reforms that would lower the presidential victory threshold, introduce proportional representation and reserve 30 percent of political leadership positions for women.

items.title: Western Europe records hottest June and July on record
items.description: Drought is gripping large parts of Europe, with soils unusually dry and major rivers running low. A strengthening El Nino could push global temperatures even higher later this year.

items.title: Trump says FIFA would be making 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino
items.description: After weeks of silence following Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup bid, his close ally Donald Trump finally speaks up.

items.title: Taiwan representative in Japan boycotts Nagasaki bombing anniversary ceremony over seating
items.description: Mr. Lee said he and two deputies boycotted because their designated seats as representatives of Taiwan were not among those reserved for diplomatic missions. Mr. Lee instead sent a lower-ranked official from Fukuoka

items.title: Germany: Interior Minister warns of 'daily' hybrid warfare
items.description: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says attacks by foreign powers have become a constant threat to Germany. His remarks come just days after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig airport.

items.title: Search for survivors underway in Colombia’s earthquake aftermath
items.description: Rescuers search for survivors in western Colombia in what is called the country’s strongest earthquake this century.

items.title: Ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
items.description: The ex-president is convicted of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war.

items.title: Truck crash in Egypt kills 18, many of them child labourers
items.description: Two pick-up trucks collide in Ismailia, Egypt, leaving 18 dead, mostly children working as agricultural labourers.

items.title: Relatives mourn victims of Pakistan avalanche
items.description: Relatives gathered to mourn the three Nepali mountaineers, Kili Pemba Sherpa, Gyalu Sherpa, and Nima Sherpa.

items.title: Fire breaks out after attack on major Libyan refinery
items.description: Libyan authorities say unknown perpetrators were behind an attack on a major gasoline reservoir west of Tripoli. The reservoir at the country’s second-largest oil refinery in Zawiya caught fire and collapsed.

items.title: Japan business mood rises as semiconductor boom lifts manufacturers: Reuters poll
Turkiye's Kurdish region greets conditional PKK pardon with relief, joy and doubt
items.description: Lawmakers on August 10 voted overwhelmingly in favour of the legislation that is aimed at advancing a peace effort between the Turkish state and the Kurdistan Workers' Party

items.title: Iceland’s EU vote: A nation divided over Europe
items.description: Security concerns, control over fishing rights and rising living costs are shaping Iceland's debate over whether to restart talks on joining the European Union.

items.title: Middle East: Trump took secret flight out of Turkey over Iran threat
items.description: President Donald Trump reportedly used an elaborate ruse to leave the NATO summit in Turkey, amid a credible assassination threat. Meanwhile, oil prices rose as hopes for a deal on the Strait of Hormuz fade. DW has more.

items.title: Europe battles wildfires and braces for another summer heatwave
items.description: As well as drought, Europe has also been battling wildfires this summer. Firefighters this week are struggling to control a rapidly expanding wildfire in southwestern Spain that has forced the evacuation of around 800 people. For more on that topic, FRANCE 24's Nadia Massih is joined by Alexander Held, Senior Fire Management Expert at the European Forest Institute.

items.title: Africa’s tech boom starts at home, By Sally Wentworth
items.description: The continent is on the move: there are more than 70 Internet exchange points across Africa; Internet penetration across the continent has grown from less than 10 per cent in 2010 to over 38 per cent today; and Africa hosts some of the world’s best technical leadership, within a thriving ecosystem rooted in civil society. items.title: Lionel Messi bids farewell to his father in Rosario
items.description: Messi and his family had traveled from Miami on a private plane and were escorted by a police motorcade to a Rosario cemetery, where a private family wake was held before the burial early on Sunday. Messi's father Jorge Messi died Saturday at a hospital in Rosario at age 68.

items.title: Live: ASX drops, CBA beats expectations with $10.9b profit
items.description: The nation's second-largest company Commonwealth Bank has announced a $10.9 billion full-year profit. The Australian share market is trading lower on fading optimism about the Strait of Hormuz reopening soon. Follow live.

items.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
items.description: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.

items.title: How a 97-year-old escaped deadly Indian floods on a banana raft
items.description: A 97-year-old's dramatic rescue captures how Assam's floods are reaching places once thought safe.

items.title: FIFA chief Infantino gets backing of AFA, South American football
